claims: The Artemis II mission is scheduled to launch on April 1, 2026, at 6:35:12 p.m. EDT from Kennedy Space Center.
The Artemis II mission carries four astronauts on a 10-day mission around the Moon.
The Artemis II crew will fly a free-return trajectory.
The Artemis II crew will perform a lunar flyby.
The Artemis II mission will splash down in the Pacific Ocean on April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II lunar flyby is expected around April 6.
The Artemis II crew consists of Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
Artemis II is the first crewed flight to the Moon since 1972.
Artemis II tests the Orion capsule.
Artemis II tests the SLS rocket.
The Artemis II spacecraft will loop around the far side of the Moon.
The Artemis II trajectory goes further than any human has traveled since Apollo 13.
Backup launch windows for Artemis II are available throughout early April if the launch cannot proceed on April 1.
